recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed unless the Extension Pack patient-animal definition regresses from 'animal extension' or HL7 decides to bring the patient-animal extension definition back into core.
issue_request: FHIR-18328 was a Published/Persuasive PA technical correction for FHIR-core Patient, raised and applied for STU3. It asked to replace 'The absence of the animal element does not imply that the patient is a human' with 'The absence of the animal extension does not imply that the patient is a human.'
initial_application: The exact wording change appears in historical commit 7bf7397f4a, which changed the Patient extension spreadsheet comment from 'animal element' to 'animal extension.' Earlier commit e3d290e779 moved Patient.animal to the standard patient-animal extension and updated the animal Patient example to use the extension URL.
additional_context: Current core Patient source remains active and now describes veterinary support through a link to the standard patient-animal extension; the example Patient/animal uses http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/patient-animal. The patient-animal extension definition itself was removed from core in dd468d4f17 as part of moving extension definitions out of R5 source, and the current FHIR Extension Pack definition has the corrected 'animal extension' comment. Legacy Patient.animal references found in core are out-of-build or historical for this issue's purpose, such as the commented-out CDA profile entry and QUICK model content.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No core source edit is needed because active core source no longer has the stale 'animal element' wording and the current authoritative extension definition outside core is already correct.
